name: HMB
summary: HMB is a substance the body makes when it breaks down leucine, an amino acid found in protein. Supplements contain a calcium salt or a free-acid form; this basic guide does not assess their benefits.
commonUses: Used in products marketed for exercise recovery.
Used in sports and older-adult nutrition products marketed for muscle maintenance.
roles: HMB is a metabolite of leucine, not leucine itself.
The body produces HMB through an intermediate called alpha-ketoisocaproate.

status.note: This basic guide does not provide a routine status test.

high.note: See the cautions below; this guide does not establish a safe upper amount.

forms.name: Calcium HMB
forms.note: Also labelled HMB-Ca; the calcium salt contributes calcium as well as HMB.

forms.name: Free-acid HMB
forms.note: Also labelled HMB-FA; this differs from the calcium salt in composition and absorption. The forms are not identical products.

reference.noUpperLimit: This basic guide does not provide reference intakes or upper-limit values.

cautions: Safety observations from studied HMB products do not establish that any amount or every formulation is safe.
Calcium HMB adds calcium to the total from foods and other supplements; it is not calcium-free.
Combination nutrition products may contain other amino acids or ingredients. Their safety cannot be judged from HMB alone.
